title: TAPP Composition Module: Aggregation
description:
The shared Aggregation block of the 2026-08-11 TAPP library (Claude Skills for TAPP/Module_Aggregation.csv), composed by 13 of the sixteen delivery tables. 3 owned fields over 4 schema paths.

GENERATED by tools/build_module_bb.py from the module's CSV and its schema-path sidecar — edit those, not this file. Requiredness follows the TAPP tier matrix: a field Basic on a side is required there, Advanced is permitted, N/A is absent from that side entirely.

This is a PROFILE, not a vocabulary: it asserts which properties a conforming procedure or analysis carries. Column F (Example / Allowed Content) is consumer-owned per the module manifest, so no enum is pinned here — a consuming TAPP may narrow a value space, never widen it.

AnalysisIdentification.title: Aggregation on the analysis
AnalysisIdentification.description: Composed into a technique detail (schema:Dataset) schema: what each run supplies fresh, because it cannot be known until the analysis happens.

schema:value.description: Whether the reported variable is an individual result or combines several, and if combined, how: the statistical model used, including any criteria governing which model is applied, and what the individual results are combined over (for example per grain, per phase within a sample, or per sample). Record 'Not combined' where each individual result is reported on its own. Record the model only; the software implementing it belongs in Data Processing Software. In the dataset: report each combined value with its uncertainty and the number of individual results it combines, and identify, for each individual result, the combined value it contributes to.

dqv:value.description: The statistic used to describe the scatter among the individual results contributing to a combined value, or to test whether that scatter exceeds what analytical uncertainty alone predicts: for example one standard deviation of the mean, or the MSWD with its probability of fit. A threshold for accepting it belongs with the inclusion criteria. In the dataset: report, for each combined value, the value of the statistic, and any further statistic (for example the standard error of the mean, or a 95% confidence interval) beside it, named.
